title: The Lift I Could Offer
scene: A friend asks for a ride to a hiking trail on Sunday. The speaker cannot drive the entire way but offers a lift to the station, then checks whether the partial help is genuinely useful.
sceneJa: 日曜のハイキングに行く友人から車で送ってほしいと頼まれる。登山口までは行けないが駅までなら送れるため、相手にとって本当に助けになるか確認する。

chunks.en: Maya asked if I could give her a lift
chunks.ja: マヤに車で送ってもらえないかと頼まれた
道中すべてを車で送ることは
それでも役に立つなら

chunks.en: there was a train from there.
chunks.ja: そこから電車が出ているのか

chunks.en: and asked, 'Would that still work for you?'
chunks.ja: 「それでも大丈夫そう？」と聞いた
勝手に問題ないと決めつけずに
「それなら大丈夫」と彼女は答えた

chunks.en: can you drop me off by eight?'
chunks.ja: 8時までに降ろしてもらえる？」

questions.question: Which split keeps 'as far as' together as a distance limit?
options: I can take you / as far as the station, / if that helps.
I can take / you as / far as the station, if that helps.
I can take you as / far / as the station, if that helps.
questions.explanation: 'As far as the station' sets the endpoint of the offered ride. Keep 'as far as' together.

questions.question: What does 'I can't commit to the whole drive' mean here?
options: The speaker does not know how to drive.
The speaker cannot promise to drive all the way to the trailhead.
The speaker has already agreed to drive the entire route.
questions.explanation: 'Can't commit to' means being unable to make a firm promise; it is not a rejection of every possible way to help.

questions.question: Why does the speaker ask 'Would that still work for you?'
options: To demand that Maya change her hiking plan.
To avoid checking the train timetable.
To make sure the limited offer actually meets Maya's needs.
questions.explanation: The speaker offers only a partial ride and checks the other person's needs rather than assuming.

speak: Imagine: a friend asks for help you can only partly provide. Read: notice the shift from hesitation to a clear agreement. Chunk: stress 'can't commit to', 'as far as', and 'still work for you' as meaning units. Understand: state a boundary, offer what is possible, then check usefulness. Check: answer the three questions. Speak (30 seconds): explain what you cannot promise, what you can offer instead, and ask whether that would still work. Final Read: read the six sentences naturally, pausing after 'I'd love to help' and lightly stressing 'still'.
review: New: 'I can't commit to ...'（〜までは約束できない）, 'as far as ...'（〜までなら）, 'Would that still work for you?'（それでも都合はつく？）. Reuse 'That works for me' (Lesson 101/104) and 'Just to make sure' (Lesson 104) in a partial-ride offer rather than borrowing or changing shop order. Unlike the last 14 lessons' bill-splitting, shopping order and borrowed camera, this scene tests the useful distinction between declining a full request and offering a smaller commitment. References: https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/far ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/commit
